summary: Czech law makes study at public universities free in the Czech language, whatever your nationality. At Charles University — founded in 1348 and Central Europe's oldest — that means a tuition-free degree if you are willing to learn Czech first.
covers: No tuition for degree programmes taught in Czech, for the standard length of study plus one year.
English-taught programmes are not free — they charge tuition set by each faculty.

No living allowance from the university. The separate Czech Government Scholarship (applications for 2027–28 ran 21 August – 30 September 2026) is the main funded route for students from eligible developing countries.
eligibility: Any nationality, with a secondary-school certificate (for a bachelor's) or degree (for a master's) recognised in the Czech Republic.
Czech at the level your faculty requires — usually tested in the entrance exam or by a language certificate.
Each of Charles University's 17 faculties sets its own entrance exams and requirements.
how_to_apply: Decide on a Czech-taught programme and check the faculty's admission requirements.
Learn Czech — many international students take a one-year preparatory course at the university's Institute for Language and Preparatory Studies (these courses charge fees).
Apply online to the faculty by its deadline and pay the application fee; most faculties close applications between February and March for an autumn start.
Start the recognition of your foreign diploma early — it must be completed by enrolment.
watch_out: 'Free' applies only to Czech-taught study. Budget a year and course fees for learning Czech first.
Deadlines are set faculty by faculty — there is no single university deadline.
Diploma recognition (nostrification) can take months and sometimes requires exams.
